messages:
arjun: Heads up — saw a steady kv-cache RSS growth on the dedicated pool after we shifted a subset of hosted traffic. Not typical OOM, more like slow resurrection of previously-evicted pages.

mike: ugh. any perf traces yet?

arjun: pasted flame & pmap snapshot below. It looks like memory is freed in our allocator but pages come back at the OS level later.

arjun: ```
# pmap -x pid
0000000000400000    132K r-x-- libredwood.so
...
rss: 42G   anon: 40G
```

arjun: jemalloc stats shows reclaimed arenas but page faults keep climbing.

jess: is this only on dedicated? or also hosted/private?

arjun: only repro on dedicated and our onprem staging box. Hosted instances (multi-tenant cloud) didn't show the growth under same load.

leah: what kernel / vm tunables differ between those envs? madvise behavior? THP?

arjun: exactly. Dedicated runs Ubuntu 22.04 w/ 5.15 and explicit madvise(DONTNEED) path. Hosted uses 5.4 variant w/ MADV_FREE semantics on our cloud base image. Onprem is RHEL 8 with hugepage compaction differences.

mike: Could be that MADV_DONTNEED causes immediate zeroing and kernel reclaims, whereas MADV_FREE leaves pages to be reclaimed lazily. But "resurrection" implies something re-mmaps or re-populates freed slots.

arjun: We think it's the interaction between our KV slot reuse + background garbage sweep + NUMA placement. Evicted KV frames are handed back to jemalloc, then reused for new KV allocations, but the pattern of reuse touches a different offset causing page fragmentation and repeated COW-like re-commits in the same page ranges. Over long contexts (50k+ tokens) this creates churn and pages end up pinned by the GPU driver on dedicated nodes.

jess: Do you have a small repro? even a load gen that wiggles prefix reuse would help.

arjun: Yes — added a micro test that simulates long-context prefix cache churn (attached snippet). When run on dedicated it grows, on hosted it plateaus.

arjun: ```python
# kv churn repro pseudocode
for i in range(1_000_000):
    put_prefix(random_prefix())
    if i % 1000 == 0: get_long_context(30_000)
```

leah: Interesting. Could be kernel ASLR/ASLR-related base addresses or allocator mmap hinting. Also worth checking transparent_hugepage=always vs madvise settings.

mike: Check /proc/pid/smaps before/after evict cycle too. If anon hugepages are being created, driver could pin.

arjun: Did that. Found some "AnonHugePages" bumps on dedicated. Also saw NV driver hold refs in /proc/<pid>/smaps that matched the hot frames.

jess: So why doesn't hosted show it? different kernel, page reclaim policy, or driver version?

arjun: Hosted uses a newer kernel + driver that coalesces and frees more aggressively, and our VM images have MADV_FREE fallback because of libc variant. Dedicated's libc + kernel combo ends up doing immediate page touches after madvise which re-commits pages sooner.

mike: Actionable items?

leah: 1) Add an allocator path to prefer MADV_FREE where available, and fall back gracefully. 2) Add a targeted smallpage allocator for KV slots to reduce cross-page fragmentation. 3) Run kernel/driver matrix tests on dedicated/onprem images.

arjun: I prototyped (1) — toggled madvise mode in runtime flags and reran churn. With MADV_FREE semantics, RSS growth stopped, churn still present but plateaued.

jess: Nice. Can we flip that behind an env var so Dedicated customers get the safe path? Might be a perf delta but better than slow growth.

mike: Also add a perf regression test: run the churn repro nightly across hosted/dedicated/onprem images and record RSS slope. Alert if slope > threshold.

arjun: Agreed. I'll push a small runtime flag: --kv-madvise=free|dontneed and add a CI matrix job. Pushed draft PR.

infra-bot: deploy queued: kvruntime/prod-dedicated -> canary (sha: ab12f3)

leah: For onprem customers we should document kernel+driver recommendations (kernel >=5.10, driver >=515, transparent_hugepage=never recommended), and include a troubleshooting KB for "slow kv-cache growth".

jess: Good. Also add observability: track "kv-evict-resurrect" metric — increment when we see an evicted frame reused that caused a minor-fault within X seconds. That will help correlate workload patterns.

arjun: I'll add the metric and the repro data to the PR comment.

mike: TL;DR — root cause is environment-specific madvise/hugepage/driver interaction plus allocator reuse pattern. Fixes: runtime madvise option, allocator fragmentation mitigation, kernel/driver guidance, and nightly regen perf test.

arjun: Yep — will follow up w/ PR link and the mini benchmark numbers. :+1:

jess: Thanks — this explains a lot of odd dedicated reports we've had.

mike: Nice catch. Ship it when green.
